title: A small bakery's cost table and its profit-maximizing output
scenario: Linden Street Bakery sells every bagel at the market price of \$3.20, a price it cannot change. The table shows its total cost of baking bagels each morning. The bakery and its numbers are invented, for practice.

stimulus.title: Linden Street Bakery: output and total cost

table.caption: Total cost of baking bagels each morning (invented data for practice)

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate the marginal cost of a bagel when output rises from 20 to 30 bagels. Show your work.
parts.sample: MC = change in total cost / change in output = $\frac{95 - 75}{30 - 20} = \frac{20}{10} = 2$ dollars a bagel.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the average variable cost of 40 bagels. Show your work.

rubric.point: \$2, with work shown: total variable cost (120 - 40 = 80) divided by 40

parts.sample: Total fixed cost is the cost at zero output, \$40, so TVC at 40 bagels is $120 - 40 = 80$ dollars and AVC = $80 \div 40 = 2$ dollars.

parts.label: C
parts.sample: The profit-maximizing output is 50 bagels a morning.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Explain your answer to part C using marginal analysis.

rubric.point: Up to 50 bagels each added bagel costs no more than the \$3.20 it adds to revenue (MC of \$3 between 40 and 50 is below MR = \$3.20), while bagels 51 to 60 cost \$4 each, more than MR, so producing them lowers profit
accept: the bakery produces where MR = MC, the last output where MR is at least MC

parts.sample: Each bagel adds \$3.20 to revenue (MR = P). From 40 to 50 bagels, MC is (150 - 120) / 10 = \$3, below MR, so those bagels raise profit. From 50 to 60, MC is (190 - 150) / 10 = \$4, above MR, so they would lower profit. The bakery stops at 50, the last output where MR is at least MC.

parts.label: E
parts.prompt: Calculate the bakery's profit at the profit-maximizing output. Show your work.

rubric.point: \$10, with work shown: total revenue (3.20 x 50 = 160) minus total cost (150)

parts.sample: TR = $3.20 \times 50 = 160$ dollars and TC = 150 dollars, so profit = $160 - 150 = 10$ dollars.
